plain.text: As Jesus left the temple, a disciple admired its huge stones and buildings. Jesus said, "Not one stone here will be left on another." On the Mount of Olives, Peter, James, John and Andrew asked when this would happen and what the sign would be. Jesus warned them not to be deceived. Many will come claiming to be him. There will be wars, earthquakes and famines, but these are only the beginning of birth pains.

"You will be handed over to councils and beaten," Jesus said. "You will stand before rulers as witnesses." The good news must first be preached to all nations. When arrested, they should not worry about what to say; the Holy Spirit would speak through them. Families would turn against each other, and they would be hated because of him. "But whoever stands firm to the end will be saved."

Jesus spoke of "the abomination that causes desolation" standing where it should not. Then those in Judea should flee to the mountains without delay. Those days would be a time of terrible distress. False messiahs and false prophets would appear and perform signs to deceive, if possible, even God's chosen people. "So be on your guard; I have told you everything ahead of time."

After that distress, the sun will be darkened and the stars will fall. Then people will see the Son of Man coming in clouds with great power and glory. He will send his angels to gather his chosen ones from the ends of the earth.

"Learn from the fig tree," Jesus said. When its branches get tender and leaves come out, you know summer is near. In the same way, when you see these things, know that it is near. "Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away."

"No one knows the day or hour, not the angels, not even the Son, but only the Father." Jesus compared it to a man who goes away and leaves his servants in charge, telling the doorkeeper to keep watch. "Keep watch, because you do not know when the owner of the house will come. What I say to you, I say to everyone: Watch!"

summary.bigIdea: Jesus warns of hard times ahead and calls his followers to stay faithful and watchful, because no one knows the day of his return.
points: Jesus predicts the temple's destruction and troubles to come.
His followers will face opposition but must share the good news with all nations.
No one knows the day or hour, so stay alert and keep watch.
summary.reflection: Jesus said, "Watch!" What does it look like for you to live ready and faithful today?
